canonical_statement: For every number field K and every smooth, proper, geometrically connected curve C over K whose geometric genus is at least two, the full type C(K) of K-rational points is finite.
domain_and_universes: universe u; K : Type u with Field K and NumberField K; C : CurveOver K stores a Scheme.{u} and its morphism to Spec K; StructureSheafH1 C.scheme : Type u is concrete pinned sheaf cohomology; the target is Prop.
hypotheses: C is smooth of relative dimension one over Spec K
C is proper over Spec K
C remains connected under every field-valued base change
for some n >= 2, the underlying additive group of concrete H^1(C, O_C) is equivalent to K^n
conclusion: Finite (RationalPoint C), where RationalPoint is the full subtype of sections Spec K -> C over the identity of Spec K.
minimal_import_basis: Each of the eight direct imports is deletion-essential in the pinned snapshot: they supply geometric base change, scheme module sheaves, properness, relative smoothness/dimension, the HasExt instance, sheaf cohomology H, NumberField, and abelian-sheaf instances respectively. No aggregate Mathlib import, projective-space construction, proof-bearing Faltings module, or external dependency is imported.
encoding_boundary: The pin has no native scheme-curve genus declaration or exposed K-linear finrank for H^1(X, O_X). The statement therefore uses the standard cohomological characterization on the actual pinned structure-sheaf H^1 type: its underlying additive group is equivalent to K^n for some n >= 2. Over a number field, additive maps are rational-linear and finite rational dimension fixes n when the usual K-action is available. This is curve-derived rather than a caller-supplied Prop or Nat, but the native K-linear/geometric-genus comparison remains explicit M3 normalization debt and receives no proof credit.

degenerate_and_boundary_cases: Cohomological genus zero and one are excluded by existence of n with 2 <= n. Genus two is included. Non-number-field bases, nonsmooth or non-relative-dimension-one schemes, nonproper schemes, and geometrically disconnected curves are excluded. The formal target adds no separate nonempty or geometrically integral premise; whether the selected primary-source curve convention entails one remains source-fidelity debt.
